Restarted kubelet with `systemctl restart kubelet`. Verified pod counts with `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep node-5 | wc -l` and restored normal write throughput.

title: web-frontend Pods stuck in Pending after node failure
description: After a node went down, `kubectl get pods -n web` showed several web-frontend pods in `Pending` with the message: "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient memory." The deployment was not scaling back up automatically.
root_cause: Memory requests for web-frontend exceeded cluster capacity, causing overcommitment and preventing scheduling of new pods after the node failure.
resolution: Reduced the memory request for the web-frontend deployment from 1Gi to 512Mi, redeployed the manifest, and added an additional 2-node pool with smaller instances. Verified that all pods are running and the cluster is now able to tolerate node failures.

title: user-auth service intermittently down due to memory overcommit
description: `kubectl describe pod user-auth-abc123` returned: "FailedScheduling: 0/2 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient memory" during a traffic spike. Logs from monitoring-stack showed frequent OOM kills in the cluster. The service was experiencing timeouts for 30 seconds.
root_cause: The user-auth deployment had an inflated memory request of 2Gi, while the cluster had only 1.5Gi available across all nodes, causing overcommitment.
resolution: Scaled down the memory request to 1Gi, updated the pod priority to high, and triggered the cluster-autoscaler to add a new node. After restarting the deployment, the pod schedule succeeded and traffic returned to normal.

title: search‑api pods OOMKilled after node failure
description: After a sudden node drain, search‑api pods started OOMKilled repeatedly. `kubectl get pods -n search | grep OOMKilled` showed many restarts. The logs contain `OOMKilled` and `Failed to allocate memory` errors.
root_cause: The search‑api namespace had a 2Gi memory request but the pod actually used ~4Gi, causing overcommit and OOM when a node failed.
resolution: Scaled down the memory request to 2.5Gi, added a dedicated node pool with 4Gi instances, and set pod priority to keep search‑api high. `kubectl edit namespace search` to adjust quota and `kubectl create -f nodepool.yaml` to add nodes.

title: payments‑service latency spikes due to memory overcommit
description: Payments‑service latency shot up to 4s. Logs show `failed to schedule pod` and `failed to allocate memory`. `kubectl describe pod payments-xyz` revealed OOMKilled events on two nodes.
root_cause: Payments‑service namespace exceeded its memory quota, and cluster‑autoscaler couldn't add nodes because of a missing pod priority annotation.
resolution: Removed the memory request from the pod spec, added a `requests: 1Gi, limits: 2Gi` to match actual usage, and annotated the deployment with `scheduling.kubernetes.io/pod-priority: 1000`. Triggered autoscaler by `kubectl delete pod payments-xyz` to rebalance.

title: Checkout API pods stuck pending on node1.example.com
description:
After the alert, checkout-api pods were showing as Pending and kubelet logs on node1.example.com contained:
"node/node1.example.com not ready: kubelet is not ready, condition: NodeReady".
`kubectl get nodes node1.example.com -o wide` returned a NotReady status for 7 minutes.
root_cause: The kubelet on node1.example.com failed to report status to the API server due to a network partition caused by a recently applied security group rule blocking outbound traffic to the API endpoint.
resolution: Updated the security group to allow outbound HTTPS to the cluster API endpoint, restarted kubelet on node1.example.com, and then drained and replaced the node with a healthy instance. Verified pods resumed normal operation with `kubectl get pods -n checkout-api`.

title: Reporting ETL service unable to schedule new jobs on node3
description: Reporting ETL jobs were queued and never started. The node3 status showed `NotReady` and the kubelet log displayed `failed to get node information: timeout`. `kubectl describe node node3` listed `NodeReady: False`.
root_cause: A recent node-problem-detector update corrupted the kubelet's configuration, causing it to hang and not report readiness.
resolution: Removed the problematic node-problem-detector pod, reinstalled the kubelet with the correct configuration file, and restarted the kubelet service. After restarting, node3 returned to Ready and ETL jobs executed successfully.

title: Search‑API nodes keep toggling ready/NotReady
description: The search‑api pods started stalling, and the cluster dashboard shows node1.example.com as NotReady for 12 minutes. `kubectl get nodes node1.example.com -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}'` returns `False` repeatedly. Logs from node‑problem‑detector show `node condition: NotReady, reason: NetworkUnreachable`
root_cause: A recent firewall rule update blocked the kubelet from accessing the etcd health endpoint, causing the node to report NotReady.
resolution: Rolled back the firewall rule to allow traffic on port 2382, then cordoned and drained the node, restarted kubelet, and uncordoned it. Verified readiness with `kubectl get nodes node1.example.com -o wide` which now shows Ready.

title: Checkout‑API pods hanging after node flapping
description: Checkout‑API requests started timing out after a flapping node alert. `kubectl describe node node2.example.com` shows `Condition Type: Ready Reason: KubeletNotReady`. Logs contain `panic: failed to fetch pod sandbox` and a stack trace from kubelet.
root_cause: The node’s network interface went down due to a faulty NIC, causing the kubelet to lose connectivity with the API server.
resolution: Replaced the NIC on node2.example.com, restarted the node, and ran `kubectl drain node2.example.com --ignore-daemonsets --force`. After the node returned to Ready, the checkout‑api pods stabilized.

title: Web-frontend pods suddenly stuck in CrashLoop due to unreachable node
description: The web-frontend pods started failing with a "node unreachable" message in the kubelet logs. The node "node3.example.com" returned "Ready: false" and the kubectl describe node output showed a "NodeNotReady" condition. The pod status shows "CrashLoopBackOff" and the logs contain "Failed to pull image" because the node cannot reach the registry.
root_cause: The node was in a network partition caused by a misconfigured firewall rule that blocked traffic to the internal registry.
resolution: Updated the firewall rules to allow traffic on port 443 to the registry IP. Ran "kubectl cordon node3.example.com" followed by "kubectl drain node3.example.com --ignore-daemonsets" to move workloads. After the node became Ready, the web-frontend pods restarted successfully.

title: ETL service hanging, node marked NotReady after VM suspend
description: The reporting-etl jobs stopped progressing and the node "node5.example.com" was marked NotReady in the cluster. kubectl get nodes node5.example.com -o yaml shows a "Ready: false" with a timestamp indicating a recent reboot. Logs from the node-problem-detector contain "VM was suspended due to storage failure".
root_cause: The underlying virtual machine was automatically suspended because the SAN storage array experienced a loss of connectivity, causing the node to reboot.
resolution: Rebooted the SAN array and restored connectivity, then restarted the VM on node5.example.com. Ran "kubectl uncordon node5.example.com" to bring the node back into service. The reporting-etl pods recovered and resumed processing.

title: Order Service PVC stalls, pods stuck in Pending
description: Order-service pods are stuck in Pending state with "Error: unable to attach or mount volume". `kubectl get pods -n order-service` shows many pods in Pending and `kubectl describe pod <name>` lists events like "Failed to attach PV: error attaching volume: volume not found". Logs from the node show `Error: cannot allocate volume: quota exceeded`.
root_cause: The underlying cloud storage provider had exhausted the quota for PersistentVolumes in the `us-east-1` region, preventing new PVCs from being provisioned.
resolution: Increased the PV quota via the cloud provider console to 2000 volumes, then deleted the orphaned PVCs that were still pending. Restarted the order-service deployment to allow new pods to bind to the newly available PVs.

title: Monitoring-stack Grafana dashboards show corrupted metrics
description: Grafana dashboards in the monitoring-stack service started showing blank panels and occasional "Error retrieving data: timeout" messages. `kubectl logs -n monitoring-stack prometheus-0` contained lines such as "storage: data corruption detected at block 0x3f2". The Prometheus stateful set was still running but with degraded data.
root_cause: A recent update to the underlying Ceph storage cluster caused a data corruption bug, which corrupted the PV backing Prometheus.
resolution: Decommissioned the affected Prometheus PV, recreated a clean PV, restored the latest backup from our backup bucket, and re‑deployed the Prometheus stateful set. Verified dashboards are now rendering correctly.

title: inventory-db pod stuck in ReadOnly mode due to PVC nearing full
description: The inventory-db pod is reporting a read-only filesystem and the logs show `filesystem full: cannot write to /data`. `kubectl describe pvc inventory-db-pvc` shows 95% usage. This is blocking new inventory updates.
root_cause: The persistent volume for inventory-db had no data retention policy and old snapshots accumulated, filling the storage.
resolution: Deleted unused snapshots via `kubectl delete snapshot old-snapshot-1` and moved archived logs to an S3 bucket with `aws s3 sync /data/archived s3://archive-bucket/inventory`. Then restarted the pod with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inventory-db` to clear the read-only state.

title: order-service experiencing slow writes after disk almost full
description: Order-service logs contain `failed to persist order: I/O error on /var/lib/order`. `kubectl logs order-service-abc123 | grep 'disk full'` shows repeated `ENOSPC` errors. The pod remains in CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: The underlying PVC exceeded 90% capacity due to unpurged temporary order data stored in `/tmp` by the service.
resolution: Cleaned temporary files with `kubectl exec order-service-abc123 -- rm -rf /tmp/*`, then scaled the PVC up by editing its YAML to request 200Gi and applied it with `kubectl apply -f pvc.yaml`. After the PVC resized, restarted the deployment (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/order-service`).

title: Checkout API Pods keep restarting – app crashing on startup
description: All checkout‑api pods in prod are stuck in a CrashLoopBackOff. `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep checkout-api` shows status CrashLoopBackOff and `kubectl logs checkout-api-5f9c6d7b8b-abcde -c app` outputs `panic: failed to load config: config file not found`. The pods fail to start repeatedly.
root_cause: The configMap containing the JSON configuration was accidentally deleted, so the app cannot find its config file at `/etc/checkout/config.json`.
resolution: Recreated the missing configMap with `kubectl apply -f configmap-checkout.yaml` and updated the deployment to mount it at `/etc/checkout`. Restarted the pods with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api -n prod`. All pods are now Running.

title: User‑auth service stuck in CrashLoop – database connection timeout
description: User‑auth pods in production are repeatedly restarting: `kubectl describe pod user-auth-7d8f9c6d-xyz | grep State` shows `State: Waiting (CrashLoopBackOff)`. Log shows `Error: failed to connect to DB: context deadline exceeded` on startup.
root_cause: The database connection string in the user‑auth deployment was updated to use the new host `db-prod-2` but the new host was not added to the service discovery, causing connection timeouts.
resolution: Updated the deployment with the correct JDBC URL `jdbc:postgresql://db-prod-2:5432/auth` via `kubectl set env deployment/user-auth DB_URL=jdbc:postgresql://db-prod-2:5432/auth -n prod`. Then performed a rolling restart with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/user-auth -n prod`. Pods now start successfully and are healthy.

title: checkout‑api pod stuck in NotReady after scaling up
description: After a recent horizontal pod autoscaler trigger, the checkout‑api pod in staging remains in Running but NotReady for 18 minutes. kubectl describe shows the readiness probe failing: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP GET /health: dial tcp 10.0.0.5:8080: connect: connection refused". The pod logs contain "Failed to bind to port 8080: Address already in use".
root_cause: The new pod image exposed port 8080 but the container already had a background process binding to the same port, causing the readiness probe to fail.
resolution: Stopped the background process by removing the stray init script, rebuilt the image, and redeployed the pod. Updated the readiness probe timeout to 5s to accommodate the startup time. After redeploy, the pod transitioned to Ready within 2 minutes.

title: payments‑service pod never starts due to missing ConfigMap
description: The payments‑service pod in prod has been in Pending for over 20 minutes. kubectl describe reveals "Failed to pull image: Error: configmap 'payment-config' not found". Logs show "java.lang.IllegalStateException: Required config file missing".
root_cause: The ConfigMap 'payment-config' was accidentally deleted during a cleanup operation.
resolution: Restored the ConfigMap from backup, applied it to the namespace, and restarted the payments‑service deployment. Verified pod status with kubectl get pods and confirmed readiness within 3 minutes.

title: Kube-proxy down, services hanging after 15‑min outage
description: After 15 minutes of silence from kube‑proxy pods, the order‑service API started returning 502s. The health check log shows: "Error from server (NotFound): pods "kube-proxy‑abc123" not found". The monitoring dashboard marked all nodes as unreachable.
root_cause: The kube‑proxy ConfigMap was missing the metricsBindAddress entry, causing kube‑proxy containers to crash on start and never register with kube‑control plane.
resolution:
Edited the kube‑proxy-config ConfigMap to add "metricsBindAddress: 0.0.0.0:10249" and re‑applied the daemon‑set: 

```
kubectl edit cm -n kube-system kube-proxy-config
kubectl rollout restart ds/kube-proxy -n kube-system
``` 
After restart, pods came up and services returned to normal.

title: ETL jobs failing due to network rules missing after kube-proxy outage
description: Reporting‑etl batch jobs failed with error: "connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.5:80". Logs show kube‑proxy pod status: "Containers in CrashLoopBackOff" and the kube‑system namespace shows no proxy pods running.
root_cause: The kube‑proxy pods crashed because the metricsBindAddress field was set to an invalid value, preventing them from starting and causing the node firewall rules to be removed.
resolution:
Restored the kube‑proxy ConfigMap to a valid state, restarted the daemon‑set, and verified that proxy pods are running: 

```
kubectl get pods -l k8s-app=kube-proxy -n kube-system
kubectl logs -n kube-system $(kubectl get pods -l k8s-app=kube-proxy -n kube-system -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
``` 
After pods stabilized, ETL jobs completed successfully.

title: Namespace quota nearly exhausted for notifications-worker
description: When attempting to deploy a new batch of notification pods, the scheduler returned `Failed to create: quota exceeded` and `Error from server (Forbidden): exceeded quota: requests.cpu=8/8, limits.cpu=16/16`. The kubelet logs show repeated `ResourceQuota exceeded` warnings.
root_cause: The existing CPU quota for the notifications-worker namespace was set to 8 CPU requests, but the new deployment requested 12 CPU requests, exceeding the limit.
resolution:
Increased the namespace quota by updating the ResourceQuota object:
```
kubectl patch quota default -n notifications-worker --type merge -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"requests.cpu":"12","limits.cpu":"24"}}}'
```
Then redeployed the pods. All pods started successfully and the scheduler no longer reports quota errors.

title: search-api pods stuck in CrashLoop due to quota limits
description: The search-api pods kept restarting with the log line `Failed to schedule pod: exceeded quota: requests.memory=4Gi/4Gi`. The deployment status showed `CrashLoopBackOff` and the event stream listed `ResourceQuota exceeded` errors.
root_cause: The memory quota for the search-api namespace was set to 4Gi, but the pod template requested 6Gi of memory, causing scheduling failures.
resolution:
Modified the namespace quota and the deployment resource request:
```
kubectl patch quota default -n search-api --type merge -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"requests.memory":"6Gi","limits.memory":"12Gi"}}}'
```
Then updated the deployment:
```
kubectl patch deployment search-api -n search-api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"search-api","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"12Gi"},"requests":{"memory":"6Gi"}}}]}}}}'
```
After restarting the pods, they stabilized and the CrashLoopBackOff resolved.

title: search-api: Pod creation failures due to namespace quota hit
description: All attempts to scale search-api pods return a 403 error: `Error from server (Forbidden): pods "search-api-xxxx" is forbidden: exceeded quota 'limits.cpu' in namespace 'search-namespace'`. The `kubectl get quota -n search-namespace` shows CPU usage at 100% of the limit.
root_cause: The CPU quota for the search-namespace was set too low after recent deployment of a new micro‑service, causing the namespace to hit its hard limit.
resolution: Bumped the CPU quota in the namespace: `kubectl edit quota search-quota -n search-namespace` and increased `limits.cpu` from 2 to 4. Restarted the failing pods to allow them to reschedule. Monitored usage for 2 hours to confirm stability.

title: payments-service: Cannot create new resources, cluster quota exhausted
description: When trying to deploy a new payment batch job, `kubectl apply -f job.yaml` fails with: `Error from server (Forbidden): admission webhook "quota-validate.k8s.io" denied the request: quota exceeded: requests for resources "pods" are not allowed in namespace "payments-namespace"`. Logs from the admission controller show `quota exceeded` errors.
root_cause: The default resource quota for the payments-namespace was exhausted due to an uncleanly terminated batch job that left dangling pods, consuming all available pod count.
resolution: Deleted the orphaned pods with `kubectl delete pod -n payments-namespace --all`. Updated the quota to allow 10 additional pods using `kubectl patch quota payments-quota -n payments-namespace -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"pods":"12"}}}'`. Retried the deployment, which succeeded.

title: Unable to deploy new notifications-worker pod – quota hit
description: When trying to scale notifications-worker to 3 replicas, kubectl apply failed with `Error from server (Forbidden): requests to create pods in namespace "dev-ops" exceeded quota "pods" (used: 24, hard: 24)`. The deployment rollout stalled and the UI shows pending pods.
root_cause: The dev-ops namespace had a pod quota set to 24 and had already 24 running pods, preventing new deployments.
resolution: Deleted an unused test pod `dev-ops/test-legacy` with `kubectl delete pod test-legacy -n dev-ops`. Then increased the pod quota to 30 via `kubectl patch quota dev-ops -n dev-ops -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"pods":"30"}}}'`. Re-applied the deployment and verified all replicas are running.

title: Payments-service deployments blocked by CPU quota in prod
description: Attempting to deploy the latest payments-service image triggered logs: `Exceeded resource quota: cpu in namespace "payments-prod" (used: 950m, hard: 950m)`. New pods stayed in Pending state for over 10 minutes.
root_cause: The payments-prod namespace CPU quota was set too low and had reached its 950m limit due to an earlier batch job that was not cleaned up.
resolution: Removed the orphaned batch job with `kubectl delete job legacy-batch -n payments-prod`. Updated the quota to 1500m using `kubectl patch quota payments-prod -n payments-prod -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"requests.cpu":"1500m"}}}'`. Re-deployed payments-service and confirmed pods are running.

title: KubeScheduler down – cluster stalls, web-frontend unresponsive
description: While monitoring the dashboard, the web-frontend stopped returning pages and kubectl get pods kept timing out. The logs showed: "error: unable to connect to the server: dial tcp 10.0.0.1:6443: i/o timeout" and the scheduler pod disappeared from kubectl get pods output.
root_cause: The kube-scheduler pod crashed due to a failed etcd connection timeout, causing it to be evicted by the kube-controller-manager.
resolution: Manually restarted the kube-scheduler deployment with "kubectl rollout restart deployment/kube-scheduler -n kube-system" and verified that the pod returned healthy. Then checked etcd health and increased the timeout setting to prevent future evictions.

title: Payments-service unable to route requests after scheduler loss
description: Payments API returned 500 errors and logs contained "Failed to schedule pod: kube-scheduler is not reachable". The service could not create new pods for scaling, and kubectl describe pods showed the scheduler was missing from the cluster.
root_cause: The kube-scheduler pod was terminated by the kube-controller-manager due to a persistent crash loop caused by an invalid kubeconfig file.
resolution: Replaced the corrupt kubeconfig at /etc/kubernetes/scheduler.conf with a fresh copy from the backup, then restarted the kube-scheduler deployment. Confirmed scheduler availability with "kubectl get pods -n kube-system" and verified payments-service responses returned 200 OK.

title: inventory-db StatefulSet stuck at generation 3, pods not progressing
description: The inventory-db StatefulSet shows 3 replicas but only 2 pods are running. `kubectl get statefulset inventory-db -n prod -o jsonpath='{.status.replicas}'` returns 3 while `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep inventory-db` shows only 2. One pod is in CrashLoopBackOff with error `Failed to mount volume`. The rollout history shows a recent update to image tag v1.4.2.
root_cause: The new image v1.4.2 contains a broken init container that fails to mount the required PVC, causing a generation mismatch.
resolution: Rolled back the StatefulSet to the previous stable image by running `kubectl rollout undo statefulset/inventory-db -n prod`. Verified the pods restarted successfully and the generation matched again. Updated the Helm chart to pin the image to v1.4.1 until the init container bug is fixed.

title: reporting-etl HPA not scaling, pods stuck in Pending
description: The reporting-etl HPA shows desired replicas 10 but only 6 are running. `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=reporting-etl | grep Pending` shows several pods in Pending state with event `FailedScheduling:0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had insufficient resources - cpu`. The StatefulSet is at generation 5, but pods are not starting.
root_cause: A recent deployment increased the CPU request from 100m to 500m, exceeding the capacity of available nodes, causing a generation mismatch.
resolution: Reduced the CPU request back to 100m in the deployment YAML and re-deployed with `kubectl apply -f reporting-etl-deployment.yaml`. Confirmed pods scheduled and HPA scaled correctly. Monitored the cluster autoscaler to ensure it can provision nodes if needed.

title: notifications-worker pods stuck in terminating state after scaling down
description: The notifications-worker StatefulSet is reporting only 1 pod when it should have 3. `kubectl get statefulset notifications-worker -n ops -o jsonpath='{.status.currentReplicas}'` returns 1, yet `kubectl get pods -l app=notifications-worker -n ops` shows one pod in 'Terminating' with a 120s grace period. Logs show `Evicted due to insufficient GPU resources`.
root_cause: GPU node shortage caused eviction of two replicas and the cluster‑autoscaler failed to spin up a new GPU node.
resolution: Scaled the GPU node pool manually via GCP console to add 2 GPU nodes, then ran `kubectl scale statefulset notifications-worker -n ops --replicas=3`. After 5 minutes all pods returned to Running state.

title: reporting-etl StatefulSet has more replicas than declared, causing data corruption
description:
The reporting-etl StatefulSet shows 5 pods while spec expects 3. `kubectl describe statefulset reporting-etl -n analytics` shows `Replicas: 3
Updated Replicas: 5`. The extra pods are running but not part of the spec, leading to duplicate ETL jobs. Log snippet: `WARN: Duplicate job detected on pod reporting-etl-5`
root_cause: A failed HPA rollout left orphaned pods that were not cleaned up because the HPA had been misconfigured with `maxReplicas=5`.
resolution: Deleted the orphaned pods with `kubectl delete pod reporting-etl-5 reporting-etl-4 -n analytics`. Updated the HPA configuration to `maxReplicas: 3`. Verified statefulset status now matches spec.

title: Web-frontend StatefulSet stuck at 1 replica, pods stuck in Terminating
description: The web-frontend pods keep showing up as terminating for over 30 minutes: `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep web-frontend` shows `web-frontend-0 1/1 Terminating 30m`. No new pods are created and the service becomes unavailable. Logs from the old pod contain `Error: unable to attach persistent volume: node does not have a matching zone`
root_cause: The StatefulSet update was paused due to a manual `kubectl patch statefulset web-frontend -n prod --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"paused":true}}'`, leaving the update incomplete.
resolution: Unpaused the StatefulSet with `kubectl patch statefulset web-frontend -n prod --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"paused":false}}'`. Then forced a rollout restart using `kubectl rollout restart statefulset web-frontend -n prod` and verified pods came up healthy.

title: Order-service HPA not scaling, pods stuck due to affinity rules
description: Order-service pods are not scaling despite high CPU usage: `kubectl describe hpa order-service -n prod` shows `DesiredReplicas: 2 CurrentReplicas: 1`. Pod logs indicate `pod "order-service-1" is unschedulable: no available nodes that satisfy pod affinity`
root_cause: Affinity rules required the pods to be scheduled on nodes with a specific label `zone=us-west-2a`, but the cluster autoscaler was not able to add nodes in that zone due to a misconfigured availability zone in the node pool.
resolution: Updated the node pool configuration to include the `us-west-2a` zone, then triggered a manual scale-up of the node pool. After the new nodes appeared, the HPA scaled the pods correctly. Verified by `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep order-service` showing both replicas running.

title: Order service pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after cluster upgrade
description: Order service containers are repeatedly crashing with "failed to create containerd task" error. `kubectl get pods -n order-service | grep CrashLoopBackOff` shows all pods in that state. The logs contain "Kubernetes client: version mismatch".
root_cause: The worker nodes in the order-service node pool were still running k8s v1.27 while the control plane was upgraded to v1.28, causing API incompatibility.
resolution: Drained the affected nodes (`kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`) and upgraded them to v1.28 using the cloud provider’s node‑pool update. Once all nodes reported v1.28, the pods were rescheduled and stabilized.

title: Notifications-worker not receiving new messages after upgrade
description: The notifications-worker service stopped polling SQS; logs show "client-go: unable to connect to cluster: version mismatch" and `kubectl get nodes` lists control plane v1.28 and worker nodes v1.27. The worker pods are in Pending state with no reason.
root_cause: The worker nodes for notifications-worker were left at k8s v1.27 after a control plane upgrade to v1.28, leading to API version conflict.
resolution: Upgraded the notifications-worker node pool to v1.28 via the cluster autoscaler, then restarted the worker deployment (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/notifications-worker`). After the nodes reported the same version, the pods started receiving messages normally.

title: Order Service TLS fails due to clock drift
description: Order Service logs show repeated `x509: certificate has expired` errors and `time sync failed` messages. `kubectl logs -n prod order-service-7d8b5f4c6-abcde | grep 'time sync'` returns `time sync error: clock offset 12.4s`.
root_cause: The underlying node hosting the order-service pod had its NTP daemon disabled, causing a 12‑second clock offset.
resolution: Enabled NTP on the node: `systemctl enable ntpd && systemctl start ntpd`. Re‑deployed the order-service pod and verified time sync with `date` command. No further TLS errors observed.

title: Payments Service stuck on TLS handshake due to unsynced node clock
description: Payments Service pod repeatedly fails with `tls: failed to verify server certificate: x509: certificate is not yet valid` and `time: invalid clock` logs. `kubectl describe pod payments-service-9f7c2 | grep 'Events'` shows `Node clock not synchronized`.
root_cause: The node running the payments-service pod had its system clock unsynced, drifting by 9 seconds.
resolution: Updated NTP configuration and restarted the node: `timedatectl set-ntp true` and `systemctl restart systemd-timesyncd`. Confirmed synchronization with `timedatectl status`. Redeployed the pod and TLS handshakes succeeded.

title: Checkout API TLS errors due to node clock drift
description: The checkout-api pods started returning 500 errors with logs like `x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid` and `tls: handshake failed`. `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep checkout-api` showed the pods were up but the service was unresponsive.
root_cause: The node hosting the checkout-api pod had its system clock skewed by 12 hours, causing TLS certificates to appear expired or not yet valid.
resolution: Enabled NTP on the node (`systemctl enable --now chronyd`), added the node to the NTP pool, and restarted the pod to resync time. After confirming `date` matched the NTP server, TLS errors vanished.

title: Order-service orders missing timestamps after hibernation
description: Orders created after a recent maintenance window were missing accurate timestamps; logs showed `order_timestamp: 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z` despite being created later. `kubectl logs order-service-xyz` included `time: 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z` which was wrong.
root_cause: The node that hosts the order-service pod had its BIOS battery depleted, causing the system clock to reset to epoch after hibernation, leading to incorrect timestamps.
resolution: Replaced the CMOS battery on the node, re-enabled the time sync service (`systemctl restart chronyd`), and rolled the pod to apply the corrected time. Verified timestamps in new orders were correct.

title: search-api pods stuck due to file descriptor exhaustion
description: The search-api deployment was showing pods in CrashLoopBackOff and logs contained "Too many open files" errors. Running `kubectl describe pod search-api-5f9d8c7f8-xyz` showed the node's FD usage at 92%. The pod restarts keep failing with "open /var/run/secrets/...: too many open files".
root_cause: The node was running out of file descriptors because a background process in the search-api container had a file descriptor leak, exceeding the system limit.
resolution: Identified the leak by running `lsof | wc -l` on the node, then increased the node's file descriptor limit with `sysctl -w fs.file-max=2000000`. Restarted the search-api pods and verified FD usage dropped below 70%.

title: user-auth service failing: "Too many open files" on node
description: user-auth pods were intermittently returning 500 errors with stack traces mentioning "ENFILE: file table overflow". `kubectl get pods -l app=user-auth` showed several pods in Pending state and logs had repeated "Failed to open socket: Too many open files".
root_cause: A sudden spike in authentication requests caused a temporary surge in open files, exhausting the node's limit due to an unclosed socket in the auth server.
resolution: Temporarily increased the node's fd limit using `sysctl -w fs.file-max=1800000`, and patched the auth server to close idle sockets. After rolling out the patch and scaling down the deployment, the node's FD usage stabilized and user-auth returned to normal.

title: ETL jobs stuck, error 503 on /status
description: The reporting‑etl pod is returning 503 errors when polling the status endpoint. kubectl logs show: "Error: ENOSPC: no space left on device, open '/var/lib/etl/output/file_12345.tmp'". The pod keeps restarting and the job queue is frozen.
root_cause: The /var/lib/etl partition ran out of inodes due to a runaway temporary file generation loop.
resolution: Cleared old temp files from /var/lib/etl, added a cron job to prune /tmp, and increased the inode allocation on the partition. Restarted the reporting‑etl deployment. Monitored inode usage and confirmed the issue resolved.

title: Notifications-worker pod crashes with inode error
description: The notifications-worker pod crashes with "node: bad file descriptor" and logs show "open('/var/notifications/tmp/msg_9876'): ENOSPC". The pod goes from Running to CrashLoopBackOff and the worker queue is empty.
root_cause: The /var/notifications filesystem hit 3% inodes left because old message files were not cleaned up.
resolution: Manually removed orphaned message files from /var/notifications/tmp, patched the worker to delete temp files after processing, and updated the deployment to mount a larger tmpfs volume. Re-deployed the pod and verified stability.

title: Search‑API pod stuck in CrashLoop due to full /var/log
description: The search‑api pod keeps crashing with "Failed to write log: No space left on device". kubectl logs search-api-7c9f5b5f7c-abcde shows repeated "disk full" errors and the pod status is CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: The /var/log directory on the node hosting search‑api was 97% full, hitting the 3% warning threshold.
resolution: Identified the node via `kubectl get pods -o wide` and ran `ssh node-01 'du -sh /var/log/* | sort -h | head -n 10'`. Deleted old log archives and cleared the log rotation backlog. Then restarted the pod with `kubectl delete pod search-api-7c9f5b5f7c-abcde` and verified it returned to Running state.

title: User‑Auth service latency spikes after disk space warning
description: Users reported authentication timeouts and the service logs contain "Timeout awaiting response". `kubectl get svc user-auth` shows the pod is healthy, but `kubectl exec -it user-auth-xyz -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/healthz` returns 500 with "database write failed: disk full".
root_cause: The node running user‑auth had its /data partition at 95% usage, causing database write failures.
resolution: SSH into the node, ran `df -h /data` to confirm 95% usage, and removed unnecessary backup files with `rm /data/backup/*.bak`. Then performed `kubectl rollout restart deployment/user-auth` to apply the clean state. Subsequent health checks passed and latency returned to normal.

title: search‑api pods stuck in CrashLoop due to inode exhaustion
description: The search‑api pods started crashing with `failed to create file: No space left on device (inodes)`. `kubectl logs` shows repeated `open /var/log/search/error.log: no space left on device`. The pod status is CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: A runaway logging daemon was creating millions of tiny log files in /var/log/search, exhausting the inodes on the node’s /var/log partition.
resolution: Deleted the stale log files using `find /var/log/search -type f -delete` on the affected node, then restarted the pod with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/search-api`. Added a cronjob to rotate logs every 6 hours to prevent recurrence.

title: user‑auth service experiencing 503s after inode leak on /tmp
description: Users received `503 Service Unavailable` errors; logs show `Cannot create temp file: No space left on device (inodes)`. `kubectl exec` into the pod shows `/tmp` has 0 free inodes.
root_cause: The authentication service’s background token cleanup script was generating a large number of temporary files in /tmp, depleting inodes.
resolution: Stopped the cleanup cron, manually removed temp files with `find /tmp -type f -delete`, and patched the script to use `mktemp` with proper cleanup. Updated the deployment to mount a dedicated emptyDir for temporary files.

title: K8s node disk space exhausted – web‑frontend pods stuck
description: The web‑frontend pods keep failing with a "Error creating container: failed to create task: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:380: starting container process caused: exec: "/app/start.sh": stat /app/start.sh: no such file or directory" and the pod status is CrashLoopBackOff. kubectl describe pod web-frontend-7f5d5c6f8-abcde shows the node has 98% disk usage on /var/lib/kubelet/pods, with node condition "DiskPressure" true.
root_cause: Container logs were not cleaned up, filling the kubelet's log directory on the node, causing the filesystem to hit capacity.
resolution: Ran `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 -n default web-frontend-7f5d5c6f8-abcde` to force cleanup, then executed `sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=1d` and `sudo rm -rf /var/lib/kubelet/pods/*/*/log/*` on the node. Updated the kubelet log rotation config to keep only 3 days. Monitored free space via `node_filesystem_free_bytes` and confirmed it dropped below 10%.

title: search‑api stuck due to node disk pressure
description: The search‑api service started returning 503 errors: "net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection". `kubectl get events -n default | grep search-api` shows "Node disk pressure". The node disk usage was 96% on /var/log/containers, and pods could not write logs.
root_cause: The container image cache on the node grew beyond the 80GB limit, and kubelet's garbage collection was not triggered because the node was already under pressure.
resolution: Executed `docker system prune -a -f` on the node to remove unused images, and added a `--image-gc-high-threshold=90` flag to kubelet to trigger GC earlier. Restarted kubelet with `systemctl restart kubelet`. After a few minutes the disk usage fell to 70% and search‑api returned to normal operation.

title: Conntrack limit hit – payment pods losing traffic
description: Payments-service pods are dropping connections and I see logs like "conntrack table full, packet dropped" and kubelet shows "Conntrack table limit reached". The pods are still running but the API latency has spiked.
root_cause: The node running payments-service exceeded its conntrack table limit due to a surge in outbound connections from a long‑running background job.
resolution: Migrated the payments-service pods to a less‑busy node with `kubectl drain node1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data && kubectl uncordon node1`. Then increased the conntrack limit on the node by editing `/etc/sysctl.d/99-custom.conf` to set `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and reloaded with `sysctl --system`. Verified with `conntrack -n | wc -l`.

title: Notifications worker hitting conntrack cap, causing message backlog
description: notifications-worker is queuing messages, and I see a repeated warning: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" in the node logs. The worker processes stall and the queue grows.
root_cause: The node hosting notifications-worker reached the default conntrack limit due to high volume of outbound HTTP requests to the external notification API.
resolution: Bumped the conntrack max on the node with `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and added it to `/etc/sysctl.d/99-custom.conf` for persistence. Then scaled the worker deployment up by one replica to distribute load, and monitored the conntrack usage with `conntrack -n | wc -l`.

title: Network interface on reporting‑etl node spamming receive errors
description: The reporting‑etl pod keeps failing to connect to the database, showing errors like `dial tcp 10.0.5.12:5432: i/o timeout` and `netlink: receive errors`. `kubectl describe node node-02` shows `NetworkErrors: 1523` on eth0.
root_cause: A defective NIC cable on node-02 was causing frame corruption, leading to high RX errors.
resolution: Replaced the Ethernet cable on node-02 and moved the pod to node-03. After verifying `ethtool -S eth0` showed errors back to zero, the pod regained connectivity. Updated the inventory to reflect the new cable location.

title: Order‑service pod stuck due to network receive errors on node-07
description: Order‑service instances on node-07 are timing out on external API calls (`connect: network unreachable`). `kubectl logs order-service-5f9c8d9d8-abcde` contains `netlink: receive errors`. Node status shows `rx_errors: 9876` on ens3.
root_cause: The network switch port for node-07 was misconfigured, causing packet drops and high receive errors.
resolution: Reconfigured the switch port to use the correct VLAN and increased the TX queue length on the node (`ethtool -G ens3 tx 4096`). After restarting the pod, API calls succeeded and `ethtool -S ens3` reported zero errors.

title: Network TX errors causing worker pod stalls
description: The notifications-worker pod has been repeatedly timing out while trying to push messages to the queue. Logs show `sai_error: interface eth0 tx error: 3/0` and `kubectl describe pod notifications-worker-abc123` reports `Network: TX errors: 12`. The pod is stuck in a CrashLoopBackOff state.
root_cause: The physical NIC on node node-12 was saturated due to a faulty cable, causing transmit errors on eth0.
resolution: Replaced the damaged Ethernet cable on node-12 and swapped the port to switch 9. After the change, `kubectl get pods -l app=notifications-worker` shows the pod becoming Ready. Monitored `sar -n DEV 1 10` to confirm TX errors dropped to zero.

title: Monitoring stack unable to send metrics after TX errors
description: The monitoring-stack pod is reporting `Failed to send metrics: network timeout` in its logs. `kubectl logs monitoring-stack-xyz456` shows repeated `socket: network is unreachable` errors. Service health checks are now failing.
root_cause: The node hosting monitoring-stack experienced high TX queue saturation, dropping packets and preventing the metrics exporter from reaching the collector.
resolution: Bumped the TX queue length on the node's veth interface with `ethtool -L eth0 combined 4096`. Restarted the monitoring-stack pod with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/monitoring-stack`. Verified metrics are now being received by checking Grafana dashboards.

title: web-frontend node suddenly stuck in I/O error state
description: The web‑frontend pod on node node‑01 started returning 504 Gateway Timeout and logs show "mdadm: array /dev/md0 is degraded". Running kubectl get pods shows the pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. The node itself reports "md0: [UUU_]" in /proc/mdstat.
root_cause: One of the physical disks in the RAID array on node‑01 failed, leaving the array degraded.
resolution: Cordon and drain the node: kubectl cordon node‑01 && kubectl drain node‑01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. Replaced the failed disk with a spare, ran mdadm --manage /dev/md0 --add /dev/sdX, and let RAID rebuild. After rebuild completed, uncordoned the node and restarted the web‑frontend pod.

title: order-service on node‑03 shows disk errors, service latency spikes
description: Order-service instances on node‑03 experienced high latency and sporadic "I/O error" messages in the application logs. The node's dmesg includes "EXT4-fs error (device dm-0): ext4_lookup: inode 123456 not found". The pod status is Running but response times exceed SLA.
root_cause: The RAID array on node‑03 suffered a disk failure causing degraded performance.
resolution: Cordoned node‑03 with kubectl cordon node‑03 and drained it. Performed mdadm --manage /dev/md1 --remove /dev/sdY to remove the failed disk, then added a new disk: mdadm --manage /dev/md1 --add /dev/sdZ. Allowed RAID to rebuild, monitored /proc/mdstat, and once healthy, uncordoned node and restarted the order-service deployment.

title: RAID degraded on reporting‑etl node – logs show failed disks
description: While monitoring the reporting‑etl pod, I saw the node status change to "Degraded" and the following log: "disk /dev/sdb: failed to respond to SMART test". The pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff and the service is down for users. kubectl get pods -n data shows the pod restarting constantly.
root_cause: A physical disk (sdb) on the reporting‑etl node failed, causing the RAID array to go into degraded mode.
resolution: Replaced the failed disk with a new one, reassembled the RAID array using: `mdadm --assemble --force /dev/md0 /dev/sdb`, and rebooted the node. After the node came back online, the pod restarted successfully and the service was restored.

title: NodeRAIDDiskFailure triggers monitoring‑stack alert, kubelet reports disk error
description: The monitoring‑stack node reported an alert and kubelet logs show: "disk /dev/sdc: I/O error, retrying". The node’s kubelet stopped accepting pods and the node status became NotReady. `kubectl describe node` shows "DiskPressure" condition true.
root_cause: The SSD (/dev/sdc) on the monitoring‑stack node suffered a controller failure, leading to disk I/O errors and node pressure.
resolution: Swapped the faulty SSD, reinitialized the RAID array with `mdadm --manage /dev/md1 --add /dev/sdc`, and ran `kubelet --node-status-update-frequency=5s` to resume health checks. The node returned to Ready state and the monitoring‑stack pods recovered.

title: Node exporter text file scrape failed on monitoring‑stack node
description: The Prometheus node_exporter on the monitoring‑stack pod stopped reporting custom metrics. I saw a log entry: "level=error ts=2026-10-13T12:45:30Z msg="textfile collector failed to read /var/lib/node_exporter/textfile_collector/*.prom" err="open /var/lib/node_exporter/textfile_collector/meminfo.prom: no such file or directory"". The Grafana dashboards are missing the memory usage graph.
root_cause: The textfile collector directory was cleaned up during a recent upgrade, deleting the .prom files that were being monitored.
resolution: I recreated the missing .prom files from the backup snapshot, then restarted the node_exporter container with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/node-exporter -n monitoring`. After the pod came back up, the metrics reappeared.

title: Inventory‑db ETL scripts stopped exposing metrics
description: After the reporting-etl job ran, Prometheus stopped pulling metrics from the inventory-db exporter. The node_exporter log shows: "textfile collector failed to read /etc/node_exporter/metrics/inventory_db.prom: open /etc/node_exporter/metrics/inventory_db.prom: no such file or directory". The inventory health panel shows no data.
root_cause: The inventory-db cron job was misconfigured and renamed the metrics file to inventory_db.txt during a recent deployment.
resolution: I updated the cron job to write to the correct file name `inventory_db.prom` and restarted the cron daemon with `systemctl restart cron`. I also reloaded node_exporter using `curl -X POST http://localhost:9100/-/reload`. Metrics are now back.

title: Prometheus config-reloader failing to apply new scrape config
description: The Prometheus pod is stuck with old scrape targets. Logs show: "config-reloader: error applying configuration: failed to parse YAML: yaml: line 12: could not find expected ':'". kubectl get pod prometheus-operator -n monitoring-stack shows restarts=2.
root_cause: A typo in the new prometheus.yaml (missing colon) caused the config-reloader to reject the config and revert to the stale one.
resolution: Corrected the YAML syntax (added the missing colon) and pushed the updated config to git. Then ran: kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-operator -n monitoring-stack to force a reload. The pod restarted successfully and new scrape targets appeared.

title: Checkout API experiencing 502 errors after config reload
description: Users hit 502 Bad Gateway on /checkout. Logs from checkout-api show: "config-reloader: error applying configuration: unknown config section 'alerting'". kubectl describe pod checkout-api-0 -n checkout-api shows last state CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: The new config included an unsupported 'alerting' section for the checkout API, which the service rejected.
resolution: Removed the unsupported section from the config file and validated with promtool. Then executed: kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api -n checkout-api to apply the clean config. The API returned to healthy status and 502 errors disappeared.

title: Prometheus Operator stuck listing CRs after token rotation
description: The order-service pod is hanging and metrics are not scraping. kubectl get pods shows the prometheus-operator pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. Log snippet: "Error listing PrometheusRules: the server could not find the service account token: no such file or directory"
root_cause: The service account token for the Prometheus Operator was rotated but the operator pod was not restarted, causing it to lose access to the token file
resolution: Deleted the stale pod to trigger a new start: `kubectl delete pod prometheus-operator-<hash>` and ensured the pod had the updated token volume mounted. Verified that metrics resumed after pod restarted.

title: Prometheus Operator fails to watch PaymentService CRs after RBAC update
description: Payments-service metrics stopped updating, and logs show "Failed to list ServiceMonitor: the user 'prometheus-operator' cannot list services in the namespace 'payments'". `kubectl get servicemonitor` returns permission denied.
root_cause: RBAC rules for the Prometheus Operator were updated but the new role binding did not include the 'get' verb for ServiceMonitors, causing watch/list failures.
resolution: Modified the Prometheus Operator ClusterRole to include `verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]` for ServiceMonitor resources, applied the change with `kubectl apply -f prometheus-operator-rbac.yaml`, and restarted the operator pod. Metrics reappeared and the error vanished.

title: Prometheus Operator failing to discover nodes, causing scrape failures
description: The payments-service scrape config stopped refreshing; Prometheus shows `no targets for instance 'payments-service'` and logs contain `error while fetching node info: failed to get node list: status code 500`. Kubernetes logs show `kubelet Service not found` for the operator. This broke monitoring for payments.
root_cause: The kubelet Service in kube-system was deleted accidentally, removing the endpoint Prometheus Operator uses to discover nodes.
resolution:
Recreated the kubelet Service with the correct selector: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: kubelet
  namespace: kube-system
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: prometheus-operator
spec:
  selector:
    component: kubelet
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 10250
EOF
`. After redeploy, Prometheus Operator refreshed node list and monitoring resumed.

title: Search API scrape config broken after node lookup errors
description: Search-api instances are not being scraped; Grafana dashboards show `No data available`. Prometheus logs display `prometheus-operator: error while reconciling node info: failed to get node list: timeout`. The `kubelet` Service was missing, so node discovery failed.
root_cause: An accidental deletion of the kubelet Service caused Prometheus Operator to fail node reconciliation.
resolution: Applied a restored kubelet Service manifest (same as above) and restarted the Prometheus Operator pod: `kubectl delete pod -n monitoring prometheus-operator-xxxxx`. The operator reloaded node information and search-api metrics reappeared.

title: Prometheus Operator stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after token rotation
description: The order-service metrics endpoint is no longer being scraped. Prometheus logs show: "Error loading service account token: open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: no such file or directory" and the pod status is CrashLoopBackOff. Kubernetes events show the pod repeatedly failing to start.
root_cause: The service account token volume was accidentally removed from the Prometheus Operator deployment manifest during a recent config update, causing the pod to fail to mount the token.
resolution: Restored the `volumeMounts` and `volumes` entries for the service account token in `prometheus-operator-deployment.yaml`, applied the change with `kubectl apply -f`, and verified that the pod transitioned to Running. Restarted the pod manually with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-operator` to ensure fresh startup.

title: Payments Service metrics collection halted – Prometheus Operator not ready
description: After the last deployment, the payments-service Prometheus scrape target stopped responding. In the Prometheus UI the status is "Unreachable" and logs contain: "prometheus-operator-0: error: failed to load config: no kubeconfig or kubeconfig path specified".
root_cause: The kubeconfig path for the Prometheus Operator was overwritten by a stray environment variable during a Helm upgrade, causing the operator to lose access to the cluster API.
resolution: Removed the erroneous `--kubeconfig=/tmp/invalid` flag from the Helm values file, reinstalled the chart with `helm upgrade --install prometheus-operator prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack --values values.yaml`, and confirmed the operator pod became ready and metrics were scraped again.

title: Prometheus Operator stuck reconciling, API requests fail
description:
The search-api service is timing out with 502 errors and the logs show "Failed to reconcile Prometheus: error retrieving ServiceAccount: the token file could not be read". Kubectl get pods -n monitoring shows the prometheus-operator pod in CrashLoopBackOff. The error message in the pod logs is
"Failed to reconcile Prometheus: service account token not found".
root_cause: The ServiceAccount token mount for the prometheus-operator pod was missing due to a mis‑configured VolumeMount, causing token read failures during reconciliation.
resolution: Deleted the problematic pod and recreated it with the correct ServiceAccount binding: kubectl delete pod prometheus-operator-0 -n monitoring && kubectl rollout restart deployment prometheus-operator -n monitoring. Verified the new pod started successfully and the error disappeared.

title: Prometheus Operator cannot reconcile Alertmanager, reporting-etl broken
description:
The reporting-etl job fails with a 500 internal server error and the log shows "error reconciling Alertmanager: failed to create secret: secret "alertmanager-main" already exists, but not owned by the operator". Kubectl describe pod prometheus-operator-0 -n monitoring shows the pod running but stuck in a reconcile loop. The error line in the logs is
"alertmanager reconcile failed: secret alertmanager-main already exists and cannot be overwritten".
root_cause: A manually created Secret for Alertmanager was not annotated with the operator’s ownerReference, causing the operator to reject it and fail reconciliation.
resolution: Removed the conflicting secret and allowed the operator to recreate it: kubectl delete secret alertmanager-main -n monitoring && kubectl rollout restart deployment prometheus-operator -n monitoring. Confirmed that the operator re‑created the secret and the reporting-etl service returned to normal.

title: Prometheus operator refusing new ServiceMonitor for checkout-api
description: The checkout‑api metrics endpoint stopped showing up in Prometheus; the Operator pod log shows: "error: failed to reconcile ServiceMonitor "checkout-api-sm" – validation failed: field 'endpoints[0].port' is required." The new ServiceMonitor manifest was applied but nothing changed.
root_cause: The ServiceMonitor YAML missed the required 'port' field in the endpoints list, violating the CRD schema.
resolution: Added the missing 'port' field to the ServiceMonitor spec and reapplied it with `kubectl apply -f sm.yml`. Confirmed with `kubectl describe svcmonitor checkout-api-sm` that the status is "Ready" and Prometheus now scrapes the endpoint.

title: Alertmanager config rejected for reporting-etl, alerts not firing
description: After deploying a new alerting rule for reporting-etl, no alerts appeared. The Operator pod log contains: "error: failed to reconcile Alertmanager "reporting-ams" – validation failed: spec.template.spec.containers[0].name is not allowed." The config was re-applied but still silent.
root_cause: The Alertmanager CRD spec contained an unsupported field 'template.spec.containers', caused by a copy‑paste error from a pod template.
resolution: Removed the unsupported container block from the Alertmanager YAML, re‑applied with `kubectl apply -f ams.yml`, and verified that alerts are now firing in the Alertmanager UI.

title: Prometheus Operator stuck, metrics not scraping
description: The Prometheus Operator pod keeps crashing with the error "failed to reconcile: authentication error: token expired" in the logs. `kubectl logs prom-operator-abc123 -n monitoring | grep -i error` shows the token issue. Web-frontend is down for 15 minutes while metrics are missing.
root_cause: The service account token for the Prometheus Operator had expired and was not rotated automatically.
resolution:
Rotated the token by re‑creating the service account and secret, then re‑applied the RBAC bindings:
```
kubectl delete secret prom-operator-token -n monitoring
kubectl apply -f prom-operator-sa.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-operator -n monitoring
```

title: Payments-service metrics out of sync after operator sync fail
description: Payments-service shows a spike in latency, and the Grafana dashboard reports "No data" for the last 5 minutes. The Prometheus Operator logs contain "Reconciliation failed: unauthorized: unable to fetch token". `kubectl get pods -n monitoring` shows the operator pod in CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: The operator's service account lacked the required permission to access the service account token, causing reconciliation failures.
resolution:
Updated the ClusterRole to include the `get` verb on `serviceaccounts/token`:
```
kubectl patch clusterrole prom-operator --type merge -p '{"rules":[{"apiGroups":[""],"resources":["serviceaccounts/token"],"verbs":["get"]}]}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-operator -n monitoring
```

title: Prometheus Operator stuck, services unresponsive
description: The web‑frontend started timing out and inventory‑db queries were failing. Prometheus Operator logs show: `error watching objects: watch error: context deadline exceeded` and kubectl reports the pod status as `ContainerCreating` with a `Failed` event. The search‑api service could not pull metrics and returned 503s.
root_cause: The Prometheus Operator’s service account token had expired, causing watch operations to fail.
resolution: Rotated the service account token: `kubectl delete secret prom-operator-token -n monitoring`, then recreated it with `kubectl apply -f prom-operator-sa.yaml`. Restarted the operator pod with `kubectl delete pod -n monitoring <pod-name>`. Metrics collection resumed and all services returned to normal.

title: Prometheus metrics scraping fails, search API down
description: Search‑api was returning 502 errors after the Prometheus Operator restarted. The operator logs contained: `error creating Prometheus: failed to get token: no valid token found` and the pod status was `CrashLoopBackOff`. Metrics were not being scraped, causing the API to misbehave.
root_cause: The token secret for Prometheus Operator was missing the `token` field, causing authentication to fail.
resolution: Re‑created the secret with the correct token: `kubectl create secret generic prom-operator-token --from-file=token=/path/to/token --namespace=monitoring`. Updated the deployment to use the new secret and restarted the pod. After verifying logs, search‑api metrics started flowing and the API stabilized.

title: Prometheus config reload failing after adding new ServiceMonitor
description: Prometheus stopped picking up metrics for inventory-db. Logs show `panic: failed to reload config: error parsing ServiceMonitor "inventory-db-monitor": duplicate job name "inventory-db"`. `kubectl get pods prometheus-0 -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'` returned Running but metrics endpoint was empty.
root_cause: Duplicate job label "inventory-db" in two ServiceMonitors caused the config parse error.
resolution: Deleted the redundant ServiceMonitor for inventory-db, kept only the primary one. Ran `kubectl apply -f inventory-db-monitor.yaml` and verified `prometheus reload` succeeded. Prometheus metrics resumed for inventory-db.

title: Metrics missing for order-service after recent config change
description: Order-service metrics disappeared. Prometheus logs contain `error: error parsing ServiceMonitor "order-monitor": duplicate job name "order-service"`. `kubectl describe svc order-service` shows correct labels, but metrics endpoint shows 0 samples.
root_cause: Two ServiceMonitor resources shared the same job name "order-service", causing a config reload failure.
resolution: Removed the duplicate ServiceMonitor via `kubectl delete svcmonitor order-service-dup`. Re‑applied the correct ServiceMonitor with `kubectl apply -f order-monitor.yaml`. Prometheus reloaded config successfully and metrics for order-service returned.

title: Duplicate timestamps from reporting-etl metrics spike traffic
description: Prometheus pod prometheus-k8s-1 logged warnings: `level=warn ts=2023-10-12T08:17:23.412Z caller=scrape.go:1372 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=default/reporting-etl/metrics msg="Error on ingesting samples with different value but same timestamp" num_dropped=24` and `kubectl -n monitoring get pod` shows both pods healthy.
root_cause: The ServiceMonitor for reporting-etl was misconfigured to scrape the same endpoint twice, causing duplicate timestamps.
resolution: Deleted the duplicate ServiceMonitor entry (`kubectl delete servicemonitor reporting-etl-dup -n monitoring`). Restarted the Prometheus pod to clear the scrape cache (`kubectl rollout restart deployment prometheus-k8s -n monitoring`). Metrics now stream correctly.

title: web-frontend metrics ingestion error during peak load
description: Prometheus logs from prometheus-k8s-0 contain: `level=warn ts=2023-10-12T08:18:01.987Z caller=scrape.go:1372 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=default/web-frontend/metrics msg="Error on ingesting samples with different value but same timestamp" num_dropped=12`. `kubectl -n production get pod prometheus-k8s-0` shows Running. No alerts from the web-frontend pod itself.
root_cause: The web-frontend application was exposing a /metrics endpoint that returned duplicate timestamps due to a race condition in its metrics exporter.
resolution: Restarted the web-frontend pod to reset the exporter state (`kubectl rollout restart deployment web-frontend -n production`). Added a quick fix to the exporter code to deduplicate timestamps before exposing them. Re‑enabled the ServiceMonitor after confirming metrics are now unique.

title: Prometheus alerts stuck, no notifications received
description:
While monitoring the production cluster, the Alertmanager logs show repeated 502 responses from Prometheus:
```
[2026-10-13 12:45:07] ERROR 502 Bad Gateway: POST /api/v1/alerts failed
```
Prometheus status page still shows all target groups as healthy, but no alert emails are sent. kubectl describe pod prometheus-0 shows a 10% CPU spike and a pending pod for Alertmanager.
root_cause: The Alertmanager cluster was saturated due to an unexpected surge in alert traffic, causing the Prometheus client to time out when pushing alerts.
resolution:
Scaled the Alertmanager deployment from 2 to 4 replicas, updated the `replicas` field in the Helm chart and restarted the service:
```
helm upgrade alertmanager -n monitoring -f values.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deployment/alertmanager
``` 
After the rollout, Prometheus resumed sending alerts and the email notifications started flowing again.

title: Search API latency spike after Prometheus alert failure
description:
The search-api team reported a 4‑second response time for `/search` endpoints. A quick look at the pod logs reveals:
```
2026-10-13T12:52:03Z ERROR Failed to push alert: connection refused
```
Prometheus metrics show a spike in `alertmanager_alerts_fired_total`. The pod was using the same node as the overloaded Alertmanager instance.
root_cause: The Alertmanager pod ran out of memory on the node, causing the kubelet to evict the search-api pod’s alert push socket, which in turn led to increased latency.
resolution:
Added a dedicated node selector for Alertmanager and moved it to a low‑CPU node:
```
kubectl patch deployment alertmanager -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"kubernetes.io/hostname":"alert-node-1"}}}}}'
```
Then updated search-api’s `prometheus_pushgateway_url` to point to the new Alertmanager service. The latency dropped back to under 200 ms.

title: Prometheus cannot deliver alerts to Alertmanager on search-api node
description:
The search‑api pod was receiving a surge of alerts but I saw the following in the logs:

"[error] failed to send alerts to alertmanager: POST https://alertmanager.svc.cluster.local/api/v2/alerts: 503 Service Unavailable"

kubectl get pods -n monitoring -o wide showed the Alertmanager pod was in CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: The Alertmanager pod was crashing due to a memory leak after a recent upgrade, causing Prometheus to time out when sending alerts.
resolution:
Restarted the Alertmanager deployment and upgraded the image to the stable v0.24.0 tag:

```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/alertmanager -n monitoring
kubectl set image deployment/alertmanager alertmanager=quay.io/prometheus/alertmanager:v0.24.0 -n monitoring
```
After the rollout the pods stabilized and Prometheus resumed alert delivery.

title: Prometheus alert loss on web-frontend after network policy tweak
description:
The web‑frontend team rolled out a new NetworkPolicy that inadvertently blocked traffic to the Alertmanager namespace. Prometheus logs now contain:

"[error] failed to send alerts to alertmanager: timeout after 10s"

kubectl get netpol -A | grep web-frontend shows the new policy.
root_cause: The new NetworkPolicy restricted egress from web‑frontend pods to the Alertmanager namespace, causing Prometheus to lose connectivity.
resolution:
Updated the NetworkPolicy to allow egress to the Alertmanager namespace:

```
kubectl patch netpolicy web-frontend-allow-alerts -n web-frontend --type=json \
-p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/egress/0/to/0/namespaceSelector","value":{"matchLabels":{"app":"alertmanager"}}}]'
```
Verified connectivity with `kubectl exec prometheus -n monitoring -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://alertmanager.svc.cluster.local/api/v2/alerts` which returned 200.

title: Prometheus dropped targets after sudden label explosion
description: The monitoring stack stopped collecting metrics for several services. Prometheus logs show "scrape error: target dropped: exceeded max number of labels 1000" and the web-frontend pod shows a 502 error on health checks. kubectl get pods -n monitoring-stack shows the prometheus pod in CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: A recent deployment added an excessive number of labels to the service discovery config, exceeding Prometheus’s label limit.
resolution: Updated the scrape_config in the Prometheus ConfigMap to remove the redundant labels and reduced the scrape interval from 15s to 30s. Reloaded Prometheus with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus -n monitoring-stack` and verified target list size is below the limit.

title: Web frontend alerts lost due to Prometheus label limit
description: After a code push, alerts in Grafana stopped firing and the web-frontend logs show "label error: too many labels". The Prometheus target list shrank to only 3 services. kubectl describe pod prometheus-0 -n monitoring-stack shows the pod is healthy but logs contain "max labels reached" errors.
root_cause: The new notification-worker image added a custom label per tenant, causing the scrape config to exceed the label limit.
resolution: Removed the per-tenant label from the notification-worker service definition, applied the change to the ConfigMap, and performed a rolling restart of Prometheus. Confirmed alerts resume and no more label errors appear.

title: Prometheus rule evals stalled, alerts missing
description: The order-service metrics dashboard stopped showing any alerts for the past 15 minutes. I saw logs like `level=error msg="Failed to evaluate rule group 'order-service.rules'" err="context deadline exceeded"` and the Prometheus UI showed `Rule evaluation pending` for several targets. The service was still up but no alerting data was being pushed.
root_cause: The Prometheus instance was running out of CPU, causing rule group evaluation timeouts.
resolution: Allocated an additional CPU core to the Prometheus pod (`kubectl patch deployment prometheus -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"prometheus","resources":{"limits":{"cpu":"4","memory":"8Gi"}}}]}}}'`). Restarted the deployment to apply the new limits. Monitored CPU usage with `kubectl top pod prometheus` and confirmed it stabilized.

title: Checkout API alerts stopped firing, Prometheus lagging
description: The checkout-api alerting was silent for about an hour. Logs showed `prometheus: error evaluating rule group 'checkout.rules': timeout: context deadline exceeded`. The Grafana dashboard displayed stale data and the alert rule was in a `paused` state.
root_cause: CPU throttling in the Prometheus container caused rule evaluation delays.
resolution: Scaled the Prometheus deployment to 3 replicas (`kubectl scale deployment prometheus --replicas=3`). Updated the resource limits to `cpu: 2` for each pod and added an HPA. Verified that rule evaluations resumed and alerts fired correctly.

title: Prometheus can’t reach Alertmanager, no alerts firing
description: Prometheus pod in monitoring‑stack reports: "no alertmanager discovered, skipping alerting". `kubectl get pods -n monitoring-stack` shows the alertmanager pod is ready but the Prometheus pod logs contain "Could not connect to alertmanager at http://alertmanager.monitoring-stack.svc:9093: dial tcp: lookup alertmanager.monitoring-stack.svc: no such host".
root_cause: The Service for Alertmanager had its selector mis‑configured, causing the DNS name to resolve to an empty set.
resolution: Updated the Alertmanager Service selector to match the pod labels (`kubectl patch svc alertmanager -n monitoring-stack -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"alertmanager"}}}'`). Then re‑deployed Prometheus (`kubectl rollout restart deployment prometheus -n monitoring-stack`) which restored connectivity.

title: Inventory‑db alerts not arriving to Alertmanager
description: Prometheus metrics for inventory-db show a high rate of 5xx responses, yet no alerts are being sent. The Prometheus alert rule logs contain "Alertmanager failed to receive alerts: connect: connection refused" and `kubectl logs alertmanager-0 -n monitoring-stack` shows a crash loop with "port 9093 already in use".
root_cause: Alertmanager pod was running a second instance on the same node due to an outdated Helm chart, causing port conflict.
resolution: Deleted the duplicate Alertmanager pod (`kubectl delete pod alertmanager-1 -n monitoring-stack`) and patched the Helm release to use a single replica (`helm upgrade monitoring-stack . --set alertmanager.replicaCount=1`). After the pod restarted, alerts started flowing again.

title: Prometheus alert queue filling up, alerts stuck
description: The alerting system stopped firing new alerts. In the logs I see `prometheus: [error] failed to send alert notification: notification queue is full`. Kubernetes logs show the container restarting with `Error: signal: killed` and `kubectl get pod monitoring-stack-prometheus -o wide` shows a pod in CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: An overloaded notification receiver due to too many alerts from a misconfigured scrape interval caused the Prometheus notification queue to overflow.
resolution: Reduced the scrape interval on the user-auth service by editing the `user-auth-prometheus-config.yaml` to 60s, redeployed the config with `kubectl apply -f user-auth-prometheus-config.yaml`, and restarted the Prometheus pod with `kubectl rollout restart deployment monitoring-stack-prometheus`. The queue cleared and alerts resumed.

title: Prometheus queue full, alerts not sending to Slack
description: After a spike in alerts, the Slack webhook stopped receiving messages. Prometheus logs contain `prometheus: [error] failed to send alert notification: notification queue is full`. `kubectl describe pod monitoring-stack-prometheus | grep -i crash` shows the pod repeatedly crashing due to OOMKilled.
root_cause: The notifications receiver was configured with a too-large `batch-size` causing the internal queue to hit its limit, leading to pod OOM kills.
resolution: Edited the `receiver-config.yaml` to set `batch-size: 50` and `max-retries: 3`, applied the change with `kubectl apply -f receiver-config.yaml`, and performed a graceful restart of the Prometheus deployment using `kubectl rollout restart deployment monitoring-stack-prometheus`. The queue now handles traffic and alerts are delivered again.

title: Prometheus crashloop causing missing metrics for payments-service
description: The payments-service dashboards suddenly stopped showing CPU usage. In the Prometheus pod logs I see: `level=error ts=2026-10-13T10:12:34Z caller=main.go:421 msg="failed to write sample: out of memory"`. `kubectl get pod prometheus-0 -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'` returns `CrashLoopBackOff`.
root_cause: The Prometheus container ran out of memory due to an increased scrape rate, exhausting the node's RAM and causing a crash.
resolution: Scaled the Prometheus container memory limit from 2Gi to 4Gi and increased the `--storage.tsdb.retention.time` to 15 days to reduce memory churn. After restarting the pod (`kubectl delete pod prometheus-0`), metrics ingestion resumed within 5 minutes.

title: Prometheus not ingesting inventory metrics after node upgrade
description: After upgrading the inventory-db node, the inventory dashboards are blank. Prometheus logs contain: `level=warn ts=2026-10-13T09:45:12Z caller=scrape.go:312 msg="scrape failed" err="dial tcp 10.0.0.12:9100: connect: connection refused"` and `kubectl describe svc prometheus-node-exporter-inventory-db` shows no endpoints.
root_cause: The node-exporter pod on the inventory-db node crashed during the upgrade and was not rescheduled, leaving Prometheus with no targets.
resolution: Re‑deployed the node‑exporter (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/node-exporter-inventory-db`) and verified that the service has an endpoint. Prometheus immediately started receiving samples again.

title: Prometheus metrics stuck, query latency spikes
description: The dashboard for reporting-etl shows a 5‑second spike in query latency and the logs contain "prometheus: received out‑of‑order timestamp". When I run `kubectl logs prometheus-0` I see the same error repeated every minute.
root_cause: The Prometheus pod was restarted during a rolling update, causing the underlying local TSDB to lose its monotonic time ordering for recent samples.
resolution: I redeployed the Prometheus instance with a fresh PVC by running `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus` and then restarted the reporting‑etl job to re‑push data. After the pod came back up, the out‑of‑order errors disappeared and query latency returned to normal.

title: Web‑frontend metrics missing after upgrade
description: After the latest rollout of web‑frontend, Prometheus stopped collecting the "request_duration_seconds" metric. The log shows "[WARN] prometheus: received out‑of‑order timestamp" and the query for the metric returns no data.
root_cause: A misordered scrape interval caused the Prometheus server to drop the metric samples due to a timestamp earlier than the last sample stored.
resolution: I patched the scrape config to use a fixed `scrape_interval: 30s` and set `honor_timestamps: true` to allow Prometheus to accept older timestamps. Then I restarted the Prometheus pod with `kubectl delete pod prometheus-0` and verified the metric re‑appeared.

title: Prometheus can't push metrics to remote storage
description: The monitoring-stack Prometheus pod started returning 502 errors when writing to the remote write endpoint. Logs show: `level=error ts=2026-10-13T12:34:56Z caller=remote_write.go:345 msg="remote write failed" err="status 502 Bad Gateway"`. `kubectl get pods -l app=prometheus` shows the pod is running but has 2 restarts in the last 5 minutes.
root_cause: The remote-write endpoint was temporarily unavailable due to a brief outage in the Grafana Loki service, causing Prometheus to fail its remote write attempts.
resolution: Scaled the Loki deployment to 3 replicas and performed a rolling restart of the Prometheus pod (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus`). Verified that remote writes resumed by checking the Prometheus metrics endpoint for `remote_write_samples_sent_total` increase.

title: order-service metrics lost after Prometheus restart
description: After restarting the order-service pod to resolve a memory leak, the service stopped reporting metrics. The pod logs contain `level=info msg="prometheus remote write: failed to connect to remote storage" err="dial tcp 10.0.0.5:9095: connect: connection refused"`. `kubectl describe pod order-service-abc123` shows the container restarted twice recently.
root_cause: Prometheus was restarted during the pod recreation, causing the order-service to miss the remote storage endpoint configuration due to a race condition; the service attempted to push metrics before Prometheus was fully ready.
resolution: Implemented a startup script in order-service that waits for Prometheus to be ready by polling `/ready` endpoint, then starts the metrics exporter. Updated the deployment with `startupProbe` to delay container start until Prometheus is healthy.

title: Prometheus remote write lagging on monitoring stack
description: Metrics from production pods are delayed by 2+ minutes. The Prometheus pod logs show: "2024-10-13T12:45:23Z ERROR [remote_storage] failed to write series: network timeout (10s)" and kubectl get pods monitoring-stack-prometheus shows the pod running but with high CPU. The alert is firing and alerts are missing in Alertmanager.
root_cause: The remote write batch size was too large for the network bandwidth, causing timeouts and a backlog.
resolution: Reduced the remote write batch size by editing the Prometheus config to set `remote_write.batch_send_timeout: 2s` and added `remote_write.batch_max_size: 5000` to keep payloads smaller. Restarted the Prometheus pod with `kubectl rollout restart deployment monitoring-stack-prometheus`. Verified that the lag cleared and alerts are now timely.

title: Checkout API metrics missing after Prometheus remote write error
description: The checkout-api service reports "No metrics available" on the /metrics endpoint for the last 10 minutes.
