Prometheus logs contain: "WARN [remote_storage] failed to send to remote: connection reset by peer". kubectl logs checkout-api-pod-123 shows the service starting up but not exposing metrics.
root_cause: The remote write endpoint was down due to a misconfigured TLS certificate, causing Prometheus to drop metrics and the API to think metrics were absent.
resolution: Updated the remote storage TLS config by replacing the expired cert with a new one in the secret `prometheus-remote-write-secret`. Ran `kubectl delete pod monitoring-stack-prometheus-0` to force a restart, and confirmed the metrics stream resumed. Added a readiness probe to the checkout-api to ensure it blocks traffic until metrics are exposed.

title: Prometheus remote write shards overflow on order-service
description: The order-service Prometheus pod is repeatedly crashing with the log line `remote_storage: too many shards: calculated 45, max 30`. The Grafana dashboards are showing gaps in request latency metrics. The pod restarts every 5 minutes. Kubectl output: `kubectl get pod -l app=prometheus-order-service -o wide` shows the pod in CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: The remote write target for order-service was sending metrics at a higher cardinality than the configured shard limit, causing Prometheus to exceed the max shards threshold.
resolution: Adjusted the `remote_write` config to filter out high-cardinality labels (`instance`, `job`) and added a metric relabeling rule to drop unnecessary metrics. Restarted the Prometheus pod with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-order-service`. Verified that the shard count now stays below 30 and the pod remains stable.

title: Missing payment metrics due to shard limit breach
description: Payments-service metrics are missing from Prometheus. In the logs I see `remote_storage: shard calculation exceeded max: 55 > 30`. The health check endpoint returns 503 during peak load. `kubectl describe pod prometheus-payments-0` shows the container stuck in CrashLoopBackOff.
root_cause: The remote write configuration for payments-service was sending all metrics including a very high cardinality `payment_id` label, exceeding the shard limit.
resolution: Implemented a metric ingestion whitelist in the remote_write config, excluding the `payment_id` label. Updated the Helm values, ran `helm upgrade prometheus payments-service -f values.yml`, and waited for the pod to reschedule. After the rollout, metrics appeared normally and the shard count remained under the threshold.

title: Prometheus rule eval fails on inventory-db alerts
description: Inventory‑DB metrics suddenly stopped firing and alerts for high CPU usage vanished. Prometheus UI shows the rule "inventory_high_cpu" with error: "cannot evaluate expression: error parsing vector selector: no matching metric found". The pod logs also contain "[ERROR] rule evaluation failed: no matches for query".
root_cause: The rule "inventory_high_cpu" referenced a metric name that had been renamed in the recent Grafana migration, leaving Prometheus unable to resolve it.
resolution:
Updated the rule to use the correct metric name "inventory_db_cpu_usage" and reloaded the Prometheus config with:
```
kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prometheus-config -p '{"data":{"prometheus.yml":"$(cat prometheus.yml)"}}'
``` 
Then restarted the Prometheus pod. The rule now evaluates correctly and alerts resume.

title: Checkout‑API rule error causing missing alerts
description:
Checkout‑API reported no alerts for failed payment attempts. In the Prometheus UI the rule "checkout_payment_failures" shows:
"cannot evaluate expression: error parsing vector selector: no matching metric found". A kubectl describe pod on the Prometheus pod shows the same error in the logs.
root_cause: The metric "checkout_api_failed_payments" was accidentally dropped during a recent instrumentation refactor, so the rule could not find it.
resolution:
Re‑added the metric to the checkout‑API exporter, re‑deployed the service, and updated the Prometheus rule to reference the restored metric. After reloading the config via:
```
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment prometheus
``` 
the alerts started firing again.

title: Prometheus missing metrics for checkout-api after scrape overflow
description: The checkout-api pod stopped receiving alerts and logs show "scrape error: 429 Too Many Requests". kubectl get pods checkout-api-xyz -o yaml shows the pod is still running but the Prometheus alert "scrape_error" is firing. Metrics for checkout-api are now incomplete.
root_cause: The number of scrape targets exceeded the Prometheus target limit, causing the checkout-api scrape config to be dropped.
resolution: Scaled the Prometheus deployment by adding a second scrape target shard. Updated the prometheus.yml to split the targets across two replicas and increased scrape interval from 15s to 30s. Restarted Prometheus and confirmed metrics restored.

title: Order-service alerts delayed due to Prometheus target cap hit
description: Order-service alerts are lagging; logs contain "prometheus: dropped targets: order-service-scrape" and kubectl describe pod order-service-abc shows the container is healthy but alerting is silent. The metrics for order-service appear missing in Grafana.
root_cause: Scrape configurations for order-service exceeded Prometheus’s configured target limit, causing targets to be dropped.
resolution: Implemented sharding by creating a separate Prometheus instance for order-service targets. Updated the Helm chart to set target_limit to 5000 and applied the new scrape config. Verified that order-service metrics and alerts are back to normal.

title: Prometheus failed to sync inventory-db ServiceMonitor
description: The inventory‑db Prometheus instance is not collecting metrics. Logs show: `level=error msg="Creating target failed" err="invalid target URL: missing scheme"`. `kubectl get svc -n inventory-db` lists the ServiceMonitor, but the scrape config is invalid.
root_cause: The ServiceMonitor for inventory-db had an invalid target URL without a scheme (http://).
resolution: Updated the ServiceMonitor spec to include the correct scheme (`http://inventory-db:8080/metrics`). Redeployed the ServiceMonitor and confirmed the target appeared in Prometheus. Restarted the Prometheus pod to reload the config.

title: User‑auth Prometheus scrape errors after rolling upgrade
description: Prometheus metrics for user‑auth are missing. Logs contain: `level=error msg="Creating target failed" err="timeout while connecting to target"`. `oc logs -n user-auth -l app=prometheus` shows repeated connection timeouts.
root_cause: A recent rolling upgrade of user‑auth pods introduced a firewall rule that blocks the 9090 scrape port.
resolution: Removed the blocking firewall rule and added an exception for port 9090. Restarted the user‑auth Prometheus deployment to apply the new network policy. Verified metrics were now being collected.

title: Prometheus compaction stalls, alerts missing on inventory-db
description:
Inventory‑DB metrics stopped showing in Grafana. The Prometheus pod logged:
"level=error tsdb/compactor.go:3243 msg="Failed to compact blocks" err="out of memory"" 
and kubectl get pods prometheus-0 -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].state.waiting.reason}' returned "CrashLoopBackOff".
root_cause: Insufficient memory allocated to the Prometheus pod caused the compactor to run out of RAM and crash.
resolution: Updated the Prometheus deployment to request 6Gi of memory and set limits to 8Gi. After the pod restarted, compactions resumed and alerts returned to normal. Monitored memory usage with `kubectl top pod prometheus-0` to confirm stability.

title: Search‑API alerts lagging due to Prometheus storage bottleneck
description:
Search‑API metrics were delayed and some alerts were firing late. Prometheus logs contained:
"tsdb/storage.go:1121: err="open /var/lib/prometheus/blocks/0000000000000000-0000000000000100: read-only file system" 
and `kubectl describe pvc prometheus-data` showed usage at 95%.
root_cause: The PVC backing Prometheus was running out of space and the underlying storage class had poor I/O performance.
resolution: Expanded the PVC from 100Gi to 200Gi and switched the storageClass to fast-ssd. After scaling the volume, restarted the Prometheus pod and observed compaction logs clearing. Verified that metrics now flow promptly to Search‑API dashboards.

title: Prometheus blocks not loading, metrics lagging
description: Prometheus pod stuck with error: "[ERROR] blockloader: failed to load block 2024-10-12 from disk" and kubelet shows 80% memory usage. Alerts for checkout-api are missing for the last 15 minutes.
root_cause: Insufficient memory allocation caused the TSDB reload to fail during block loading.
resolution: Scaled the prometheus pod from 2Gi to 4Gi RAM: kubectl patch deployment monitoring-stack-prometheus -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"prometheus","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"4Gi"}}}]}}}' and restarted the pod. Verified blocks loaded successfully.

title: Search API alerts dropping due to Prometheus reload failures
description: Prometheus shows repeated "unable to reload TSDB: memory exhausted" messages and search-api alert rule evaluations are delayed. `kubectl describe pod monitoring-stack-prometheus` shows memory requests at 1Gi but limits at 2Gi, causing OOM kills.
root_cause: Prometheus pod memory limit too low for the current block size, leading to frequent reload failures.
resolution: Increased the pod memory limit to 3Gi and updated the PVC to use a fast SSD storageClass: kubectl patch pvc monitoring-stack-prometheus-logs -p '{"spec":{"storageClassName":"fast-ssd"}}'. Restarted the pod, after which reloads succeeded and alerts returned to normal.
